patients.summary: Software engineer who joined at 21 and over the next years is found to have NF1, hereditary angioedema type I and PiZZ alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with early emphysema, then a stage IIB nonseminomatous testicular germ cell tumor found through PTHrP-mediated hypercalcemia. Two later crashes: a T4 fracture with incomplete cord injury and neurogenic shock (2024), and a left pulmonary contusion needing VATS (2026).

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is 21, just moved to Belchertown for a job at a software company, needs a primary doctor. Insurance BCBS PPO through employer, card info taken. No prior records to send, says he hasn't really had a doctor since his pediatrician. Booked new patient physical 9/10 at 8:40. Membership agreement emailed.

documents.title: New Patient Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
21 yo man new to the area, here to set up primary care. No complaints. Last regular care was with his pediatrician in high school; no hospitalizations, no surgeries, no daily meds. NKDA.

Social: software engineer, started a new job last month, works mostly remote. Single, lives alone in an apartment. Never smoked, no vaping, no drugs. Beer or wine on weekends, 2-3 drinks. Runs and rides a bike a few times a week.

Family: father died at 45 of liver failure; the family has always put it down to his drinking. Maternal grandfather has high blood pressure. Mother living, he isn't aware of medical problems for her. No siblings mentioned.

ROS negative across systems.

Exam: thin, well appearing. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no nodes or thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin: no rashes. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P: healthy young adult.
- Screening: CBC, CMP, lipids, HIV and hep C once today.
- Tdap given, last one he recalls was middle school.
- PHQ-2 negative.
- Flu shot when it arrives in October.
RTC one year for physical.

orders.reason: recurrent episodes of swelling without hives

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
23 yo here for his yearly exam, first in-person in a while. Feels fine. Fully vaccinated for COVID in the spring.

Two things came up:
1) I noticed spots on his skin during the exam (below). He says he has had them as long as he can remember and his mom has the same kind, as does one of her brothers. His father didn't.
2) When asked about anything else, he describes episodes over roughly the last year where his lip, a hand, or once his genitals swelled up over a few hours and then went down on its own over two or three days. No hives, no itching. Separately he has had a few bad bouts of crampy belly pain. He hadn't connected them and didn't come in for any of them.

Meds none. NKDA. Social unchanged: software engineer, never smoker, weekend drinks.

Exam: thin, well. Skin: many flat hyperpigmented macules scattered over the trunk, arms and legs; clusters of small brown freckle-type spots in both axillae and the groin. No subcutaneous nodules felt. Mouth: no mucosal lesions. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No swelling today. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P:
1. Neurofibromatosis type 1, clinical diagnosis: the macules plus axillary and inguinal freckling, and a mother with the same findings. BP normal. Ophthalmology referral for slit-lamp exam. Discussed what NF1 means and the yearly skin and BP checks.
2. Recurrent swelling episodes without urticaria plus abdominal pain bouts - want allergy/immunology to evaluate for a bradykinin-type angioedema rather than me ordering piecemeal. Referral placed. Come in or go to ED if throat or tongue swells.
3. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP today. Flu in fall.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Jacob, bloodwork from Friday is all normal. The referral coordinator will call you with ophthalmology and allergy appointments.

documents.title: RE: Your labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks. Allergy can't see me until late August, is that ok? Nothing's swollen since.

documents.title: RE: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's fine. If you get swelling in your tongue or throat, or trouble breathing, go straight to the ED.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Outside ophthalmology practice. Date of visit: 07/20/2021.
Reason: referred by PCP, possible NF1, slit-lamp exam requested.
Ocular history: none; no glasses. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
VA 20/20 OD and OS uncorrected. Pupils equal, no APD. Color plates full. Confrontation fields full.
Slit lamp: lids and lashes normal; conjunctiva quiet; corneas clear; irides without Lisch nodules or other nodules OU; lenses clear.
Dilated fundus: discs pink and sharp, cup-to-disc 0.3 OU, no optic nerve pallor or swelling; maculae and periphery normal; no choroidal lesions.
Impression: normal eye exam, no ocular features of NF1 at this time.
Plan: repeat exam yearly given the diagnosis. Thank you for the referral.

conditions.label: Hereditary angioedema
conditions.note: Type I, C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency

medications.sig: Inject 30 mg under the skin at onset of an attack; may repeat every 6 hours, no more than 3 doses in 24 hours

documents.title: Allergy and Immunology Consultation
documents.author: allergy and immunology
documents.body:
Outside allergy and immunology group. Date of visit: 08/23/2021. Addendum with results 08/31/2021.

Referred by his PCP after his June physical for recurrent swelling.

History: over about the past twelve months he has had a number of episodes of localized swelling - lips, either hand, and the genitals. Each comes on gradually over several hours and clears without treatment in two to three days. Apart from these he describes three earlier bouts of severe crampy abdominal pain with bloating and watery diarrhea; no fever, no blood. Never hives, wheeze or itch with any of them. No food triggers he can name, and he takes no medications, so no ACE inhibitor or new drug exposure.
Family: his mother and one maternal uncle both had episodes of facial swelling as young people that were never explained.
Meds: none daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: software engineer; never smoker; weekend alcohol.

Vitals stable. Exam unremarkable today; no swelling, skin clear apart from his known pigmented macules.

Labs drawn today, resulted 8/30: C4 6 mg/dL (ref 14-40); C1 esterase inhibitor antigen 7 mg/dL (ref 21-39); C1 inhibitor function 22% (ref >67%).

Assessment: hereditary angioedema type I (low C1 inhibitor level and function with low C4), consistent with his non-urticarial swelling and the abdominal attacks.

Plan:
- Icatibant 30 mg subcut at onset of an attack, may repeat every 6 h to max 3 doses/24 h. Taught self-injection in clinic. Keep two syringes on hand.
- Any throat tightness, voice change or trouble swallowing: give a dose and call 911.
- Avoid ACE inhibitors and estrogen-containing products.
- First-degree relatives should be tested; mother especially.
- Procedures and surgery need pre-procedure prophylaxis; contact us beforehand.
- Return in one year, sooner if attacks become frequent; long-term prophylaxis can be discussed then.

documents.title: Prior authorization - icatibant
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Specialty pharmacy faxed a PA request for icatibant 30 mg syringes. Prescriber is the allergist, but the plan sent it here as PCP of record. Called allergy office - they are submitting it with the lab results. Faxed back that allergy is handling.

documents.title: RE: Used my icatibant
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Glad it worked. The allergist manages that prescription, so we sent their office a note this morning asking for the refill to go to your specialty pharmacy. Let us know if you hear nothing by Friday.

orders.reason: progressive exertional dyspnea, low resting saturation

documents.title: Office Visit - Dyspnea
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Says his stamina has been slipping for a couple of years and he blamed working from home. Now gets winded going up one flight of stairs to his apartment, and he gave up running last fall. No wheezing, no chest pain, no cough or sputum. No fevers. No leg swelling. Never smoked or vaped. One HAE lip attack in March, treated.

O: SpO2 93% RA at rest, which is low for him and for his age. Thin. Lungs: breath sounds diminished throughout, no wheeze or crackles. Heart RRR, no murmur. No clubbing, no edema.

A/P: progressive exertional dyspnea in a 24 yo never smoker with low resting saturation. Needs a full pulmonary evaluation - referring to pulmonology, asked for the first available. Return precautions reviewed.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Lungs are hyperinflated with bilateral hyperlucency. Several large bullae in both lower lobes. No consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Mediastinum normal. Bones intact.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral hyperlucency with several large lower-lobe bullae.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group. Date of visit: 06/20/2022.

Reason: referred by PCP for progressive dyspnea.

HPI: 24-year-old man with NF1 and hereditary angioedema. Over roughly two years his exercise tolerance has gone down; he now gets short of breath after a single flight of stairs. No wheeze, chest pain or cough. Never smoker, no vaping, no recreational drugs. Drinks socially on weekends. No recent travel. Works for a software company.
Meds: icatibant as needed. Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father died at 45 of liver failure, which the family attributes to alcohol.

Exam: thin young man, slightly tachypneic at rest. SpO2 92% on room air. Chest a little barrel-shaped; percussion mildly hyperresonant on both sides. Breath sounds decreased with a prolonged expiratory phase, no wheezes, no crackles. No clubbing. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen normal. No leg edema.

Imaging today: chest x-ray with bilateral hyperlucency and several large bullae in the lower lobes.

Impression: lower-lobe predominant bullous lung disease in a young never smoker, strongly suggesting alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency. We expect the PFTs to show obstruction and reduced diffusion.

Plan: alpha-1 antitrypsin level and phenotype drawn today; full PFTs and CT chest; genetic counseling referral. He is understandably worried about the long term and what this means for his oxygen levels; we spent time on it and will go through results together.

medications.sig: 60 mg/kg IV once weekly by home infusion

medications.drug: NDA020983 60 ACTUAT albuterol 0.09 MG/ACTUAT Metered Dose Inhaler
medications.sig: Inhale 2 puffs every 4 to 6 hours as needed for shortness of breath

reports.text: Spirometry, lung volumes and diffusing capacity. Good effort, acceptable and repeatable. FEV1 1.92 L (45% predicted). FVC 4.10 L (79% predicted). FEV1/FVC 0.47. No significant change after albuterol. DLCO 48% predicted.
reports.conclusion: Moderately severe airflow obstruction without significant bronchodilator response; reduced diffusing capacity.

reports.text: Noncontrast CT of the chest. Panlobular emphysema, predominantly in the lower lobes, with several large bullae in both lower lobes, the largest 6.1 cm in the left lower lobe. Upper lobes relatively spared. No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or effusion. Airways patent. Heart and great vessels normal. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lower-lobe predominant panlobular emphysema with large bullae; no nodules.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group. Date of visit: 07/25/2022.

Results reviewed with him today:
- Alpha-1 antitrypsin 22 mg/dL (ref 100-190); phenotype PiZZ.
- PFTs 7/6: FEV1 1.92 L (45%), FVC 4.10 L (79%), FEV1/FVC 0.47, no bronchodilator response; DLCO 48%.
- CT chest 7/6: panlobular emphysema, lower-lobe predominant, multiple large bullae, largest 6.1 cm LLL; no nodules.

Assessment: severe alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (PiZZ) with early-onset panacinar emphysema and moderately severe obstruction.

Plan:
- Start weekly IV alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor augmentation, 60 mg/kg, through home infusion. Insurance approval underway; first infusion expected early August.
- Tiotropium 2 inhalations daily; albuterol 2 puffs q4-6h prn.
- Absolutely no smoking or vaping, including secondhand where he can help it; keep alcohol modest given liver risk.
- To PCP: please give pneumococcal and hepatitis A and B vaccines, and check liver tests and a liver ultrasound yearly.
- Genetic counseling referral placed.
- Return in 6 months with spirometry.

documents.title: Home infusion paperwork
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Home infusion company called for his most recent H&P and med list to complete their intake for the weekly alpha-1 infusions ordered by pulmonology. Last office note and allergy list faxed with patient's verbal OK. First nurse visit at his home is 8/4.

documents.title: Genetic Counseling
documents.author: medical genetics
documents.body:
Genetic counseling session, 08/15/2022, by video.

Indication: PiZZ alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with emphysema.

Pedigree: his father died at 45 of liver failure that was attributed to drinking. In the weeks since his diagnosis his mother obtained his father's old medical records: his father had been diagnosed with PiZZ alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency and emphysema in his late thirties. Jacob was not told at the time. His mother and a maternal uncle had unexplained facial swelling when younger and have pigmented skin spots like his. He also carries diagnoses of NF1 and hereditary angioedema type I, both dominant conditions, which we reviewed briefly; the angioedema pattern points to his mother's side.

Counseling: alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency is autosomal recessive; he inherited a Z allele from each parent, so his mother is at least a carrier. Any future children would all carry one Z allele; their risk of being affected depends on a partner's status, and partner testing is simple. Discussed liver involvement as well as lung.
Plan: mother offered carrier testing; letter provided for relatives. Follow up as needed.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up - Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over the new diagnosis and get the vaccines pulmonology asked for.

Pulm letters reviewed: AAT 22, PiZZ; FEV1 45% predicted, DLCO 48%; CT with lower-lobe panlobular emphysema and large bullae. Now on weekly augmentation at home (third infusion this week, no reactions), tiotropium daily, albuterol about once a week on the stairs.

Family news: genetics session found that his father had the same alpha-1 diagnosis with emphysema. And after the allergist's advice last year his mother finally got tested and was diagnosed with hereditary angioedema type I this spring.

He's taking it in stride but admits it's a lot at 24. Still working full time. No smoking exposure at home or work. Cut back to a couple of drinks on weekends.

Exam: SpO2 93% RA. Lungs diminished, prolonged expiration, no wheeze. Port-free, uses peripheral IV for infusions; no arm phlebitis.

A/P:
1. AATD PiZZ with panlobular emphysema: per pulm. PCV20 today. Hep A/B combined series started today, #2 in a month, #3 at 6 months. Hepatic panel today; liver ultrasound ordered. Yearly liver tests going forward. Flu every fall.
2. HAE type I: one attack in March, icatibant worked. Allergy follows.
3. NF1: skin unchanged, BP normal.
RTC for physical early next year.

reports.text: Liver normal in size and echotexture with smooth contour, no focal lesion. Gallbladder normal without stones or wall thickening. Common bile duct 3 mm. Portal vein patent with hepatopetal flow. Spleen normal in size. Right kidney normal.
reports.conclusion: Normal liver and right upper quadrant ultrasound.

documents.title: Liver results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news, Jacob: your liver blood tests from August and yesterday's ultrasound are both normal. We'll repeat the blood tests once a year and the ultrasound with your pulmonologist's schedule. Hep A/B shot #2 is due around the end of the month.

documents.title: Allergy and Immunology Follow-up
documents.author: allergy and immunology
documents.body:
Outside allergy and immunology group. Date of visit: 09/19/2022.
HAE type I, one-year follow-up. Two attacks in the past year (lip in March, hand in July), each treated with a single icatibant dose with good response. No laryngeal or abdominal attacks since diagnosis. New since last visit: PiZZ alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency on weekly augmentation; no interaction concerns. His mother has now been diagnosed with HAE type I as well.
Exam normal.
Plan: continue icatibant on demand; two syringes on hand at all times. Attack frequency does not warrant long-term prophylaxis right now. Pre-procedure prophylaxis plan on file for any surgery or dental work. Return 1 year.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Hep A/B #2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hep A/B combined vaccine dose 2 of 3, R deltoid. Dose 1 8/30 without reaction. Dose 3 due late Feb, will do with his physical.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Vaccines
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu L arm, bivalent Pfizer booster R arm. Pt reports infusions going fine weekly at home. Observed 15 min.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group. Date of visit: 01/17/2023.
AATD PiZZ with panlobular emphysema, 6 months on weekly augmentation, tiotropium and as-needed albuterol. Feels his breathing is about the same, maybe slightly better on stairs with the inhaler. No exacerbations. Office spirometry stable compared with July. SpO2 93% RA. Exam unchanged.
Plan: continue all three. Walking program encouraged. Return in 6 months.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
25 yo, annual exam. Breathing stable per him and per pulm's January letter. Infusions weekly, no problems. One small HAE hand swelling in the fall, icatibant x1. Mood ok; some worry about the future with the lungs, sleeping fine. Interviewing for a new job, hoping to start in the spring.

Meds: alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor weekly IV (home infusion), tiotropium daily, albuterol prn, icatibant prn. NKDA.

Exam: SpO2 94% RA. Thin, comfortable. Skin: pigmented macules and axillary/inguinal freckling unchanged, no new nodules. Lungs diminished, prolonged expiration. Heart RRR. Abdomen soft, no liver edge. No edema.

A/P:
1. AATD with emphysema: stable. Labs with LFTs today.
2. HAE type I: on-demand therapy, allergy following.
3. NF1: stable skin, normal BP; ophthalmology yearly.
4. Health maintenance: Hep A/B dose 3 today, series complete. PHQ-9 3, GAD-7 4. Lipids today. Flu and COVID up to date.
RTC 1 yr, sooner prn.

documents.title: Labs from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All of yesterday's labs are normal, including liver tests and cholesterol. Your hep A/B series is complete. Good luck with the job search.

documents.title: Employer health screening labs
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Copy of new-employee health screening labs brought in by patient, collected 06/07/2023 at an outside lab. Flagged: calcium 12.1 mg/dL (ref 8.6-10.3). Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL. Remaining chemistry within range. Scanned for PCP review at today's visit.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - High Calcium
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Started the new job in May. Their onboarding health package included bloodwork on 6/7 and his calcium came back high, so he brought the printout. He feels completely well. Exercising regularly again - walking hills and light weights. No excess thirst or urination, no kidney stones ever, no fractures. No calcium or vitamin D supplements, no antacids. Breathing at his baseline; infusions weekly; no HAE attacks since the fall.

O: SpO2 93% RA. Well appearing, thin. Lungs diminished as before. Heart RRR. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin unchanged.
Outside labs 6/7: Ca 12.1 (8.6-10.3), creatinine 0.9.

A/P: hypercalcemia, asymptomatic, kidney function normal. Not on anything that raises calcium. Need to confirm and sort out PTH-dependent vs not.
- Repeat calcium, intact PTH, PTHrP, 25-OH vitamin D today.
- Plenty of fluids meanwhile.
- Will call with results.

orders.order: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast

documents.title: Results call - calcium workup
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with results from 6/19: Ca 12.3, PTH 8 (low, ref 15-65), PTHrP 4.8 pmol/L (high, ref <2.0), 25-OH D 32. So the parathyroids are appropriately shut off and a PTH-related protein is driving the calcium. Explained that this pattern usually comes from a tumor and we need imaging now rather than later. He was quiet but asked good questions. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast ordered urgently - scheduled for Friday 6/23. Keep drinking 2-3 L a day; ED for confusion, vomiting, can't keep fluids down.

reports.text: CT of the chest with IV contrast. Lower-lobe predominant panlobular emphysema with large bilateral lower-lobe bullae, unchanged from July 2022. No pulmonary nodule or mass. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary lymphadenopathy. No effusion. Heart normal in size. No bone lesion.
reports.conclusion: Known emphysema and bullae. No thoracic adenopathy or nodule.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: CT of the abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast. A 3.6 cm enlarged interaortocaval lymph node at the level of the renal hilum. No other retroperitoneal, mesenteric or pelvic lymphadenopathy. Liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenal glands and kidneys normal. No hydronephrosis. Bowel normal. Bladder normal. No ascites. No bone lesion.
reports.conclusion: Isolated 3.6 cm interaortocaval lymph node. Correlate with testicular exam and tumor markers.

documents.title: CT result call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed CT with pt: one enlarged lymph node, 3.6 cm, between the aorta and IVC; lungs show his known emphysema only, nothing else. In a 25 yo man that node location makes me think first of a testicular primary. He has not noticed any testicular change. Booked in office Monday 8:00 for exam, ultrasound and tumor markers. He'll bring his mother.

reports.text: Grayscale and color Doppler ultrasound of the scrotum. Right testis contains a 2.6 cm heterogeneous, predominantly hypoechoic intratesticular mass with internal vascularity. Remaining right testicular parenchyma normal. Left testis normal in size and echotexture without mass. Epididymides normal. No hydrocele or varicocele.
reports.conclusion: 2.6 cm solid right intratesticular mass, suspicious for germ cell tumor. Normal left testis.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

orders.reason: right testicular mass with retroperitoneal node, urgent

documents.title: Office Visit - Testicular Exam
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with his mother after Friday's CT. No pain or swelling he has noticed, no breast tenderness, no back pain. Feels well.

Exam: SpO2 93% RA. Abdomen soft, no palpable mass. GU: in the right testis a firm, nontender nodule roughly 2-3 cm; left testis normal; no hydrocele; no inguinal nodes. No gynecomastia. Lungs at his baseline.

Scrotal ultrasound obtained same morning: 2.6 cm solid hypoechoic vascular mass in the right testis, left normal.

A/P: right testicular mass with an isolated 3.6 cm interaortocaval node and PTHrP-mediated hypercalcemia - presumed testicular germ cell tumor with nodal spread until proven otherwise.
- AFP, beta-hCG, LDH drawn now, before any surgery.
- Urgent urology referral; spoke with the urologist on call, he will be seen this week.
- Calcium 12.3 last week; he is asymptomatic and drinking well; recheck with urology's pre-op labs.
- Messaged allergy: he will need their pre-op HAE prophylaxis.
Long talk with him and his mother. They have a good grasp of the next steps.

documents.title: Tumor markers
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Jacob, the markers came back: AFP 486, hCG 2,140 and LDH 298, all raised. This fits a nonseminoma type of germ cell tumor, which is very treatable even when it has reached a lymph node. Urology has you Thursday 6/29; they will plan surgery and get oncology involved. Call me any time.

documents.title: RE: Tumor markers
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks for moving so fast on all of this. My mom is coming with me Thursday.

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of descended right testis
conditions.note: mixed nonseminomatous germ cell tumor, stage IIB, with PTHrP-mediated hypercalcemia

reports.text: Specimen: right testis and spermatic cord, radical inguinal orchiectomy. Gross: testis 4.6 x 3.0 x 2.6 cm with a 2.8 cm tan-white, focally hemorrhagic intratesticular mass. Microscopic: mixed germ cell tumor composed of embryonal carcinoma and yolk sac tumor. Tumor confined to the testis; tunica albuginea, rete testis, epididymis and spermatic cord uninvolved. No lymphovascular invasion. Spermatic cord margin negative.
reports.conclusion: Right testis: mixed nonseminomatous germ cell tumor (embryonal carcinoma and yolk sac tumor), 2.8 cm, confined to testis, no lymphovascular invasion, cord margin negative (pT1).

documents.title: Urology - Operative Report and Pathology
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology group. Seen 06/29/2023; surgery 07/06/2023 at a regional hospital.
Pre-op: right testicular mass, interaortocaval node 3.6 cm, AFP 486, hCG 2,140, LDH 298, calcium 12.3. HAE type I: C1 inhibitor concentrate given 1 hour before incision per his allergist's plan.
Procedure: right radical inguinal orchiectomy through a right inguinal incision with high ligation of the spermatic cord. EBL minimal. No complications; no angioedema. Home same day.
Pathology (signed 7/10): mixed nonseminomatous germ cell tumor (embryonal carcinoma, yolk sac tumor), 2.8 cm, organ-confined, no LVI, margin negative.
Stage with the 3.6 cm node: IIB. Post-op markers to be drawn 7/13. Referred to medical oncology; appointment 7/17.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 8 hours as needed for nausea during chemotherapy

documents.title: Medical Oncology Consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside medical oncology group. Date of visit: 07/17/2023.

25-year-old man with a right testicular mixed nonseminomatous germ cell tumor (embryonal carcinoma and yolk sac), s/p right radical inguinal orchiectomy 7/6, with an isolated 3.6 cm interaortocaval node on CT and no thoracic disease. Presented through asymptomatic hypercalcemia with suppressed PTH and raised PTHrP. Also AATD PiZZ with emphysema on augmentation (FEV1 45%, DLCO 48%), HAE type I and NF1.
Markers pre-op: AFP 486, hCG 2,140, LDH 298. Post-op 7/13: AFP 210, hCG 380, calcium 11.6.

Stage IIB, S1. IGCCCG good risk.

Plan: four cycles of etoposide and cisplatin (EP), 21-day cycles, starting 7/24. Bleomycin is deliberately omitted because of his emphysema and low diffusing capacity; EP x4 is the equivalent good-risk regimen. Ondansetron as needed plus our standard premeds. Hydration with each cycle; we expect the calcium to normalize as the tumor responds. CBC and CMP each cycle; markers each cycle. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis after cycle 4. Allergy aware for any line placement.

documents.title: Oncology - Cycle 2
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service: 12/07/2024 (Saturday).
CC: motorcycle crash.
HPI: 27-year-old man, unhelmeted motorcyclist, thrown from the bike and landed on his back; brought by EMS on a backboard. History of AATD with emphysema, hereditary angioedema type I, NF1, and treated testicular cancer.
Meds per patient: weekly alpha-1 infusions, tiotropium, albuterol, icatibant prn. NKDA.
Arrival vitals: BP 85/50, HR 48, RR 22, T 35.6 C, SpO2 92% on room air; breathing shallow.
Exam: GCS 15. No head or facial injury. Flaccid paralysis of both legs with absent sensation below the nipple line. Abdomen soft. Bladder distended; Foley placed, 800 mL drained.
CT spine: T4 fracture with cord injury. CT head negative.
Assessment: neurogenic shock (hypotension with bradycardia) from T4 spinal cord injury; hypoxemia with shallow breathing.
ED course: fluids, norepinephrine started, atropine for bradycardia, supplemental oxygen, blood cultures drawn, spine precautions. Neurosurgery and trauma at bedside. To ICU.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital, trauma service. Admitted 12/07/2024, discharged 12/18/2024 to inpatient rehabilitation.

Diagnoses: T4 vertebral fracture with spinal cord injury (incomplete); neurogenic shock, resolved; hypoxemia, resolved.

Course:
- ICU 12/7-12/13. Neurogenic shock managed with fluids, norepinephrine and atropine; MAP goals for cord perfusion. Blood cultures no growth; no infectious source, septic shock excluded. Pressors off 12/11. Oxygen weaned to room air 12/11.
- 12/8: posterior instrumented fusion T2-T6 with T4 decompressive laminectomy (neurosurgery). HAE: C1 inhibitor concentrate before surgery per his allergist's protocol; no swelling. No complications.
- After spinal shock resolved, exam showed preserved sacral sensation and partial motor function below T4: incomplete injury.
- Augmentation infusions held during admission, to resume in rehab.
- Foley in place at discharge, voiding trial planned in rehab.

Discharge to inpatient rehabilitation on 12/18. Meds: oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325 as needed, tiotropium, albuterol prn, icatibant prn; augmentation to resume. Neurosurgery follow-up 6 weeks after rehab discharge.

Says he has a little movement in his feet today. Allergy was contacted by the hospital for his HAE before surgery. Told her we'll request records and see him after discharge. Routed to PCP.

Progress: steady return of lower-extremity strength and sensation. Foley removed 12/30, voiding spontaneously with low post-void residuals. Transfers independent. Walking 150 feet with a rolling walker at discharge; stairs with rail and supervision.
Weekly augmentation infusions resumed 12/26. No HAE attacks.
Pain: oxycodone-acetaminophen tapered and stopped at discharge; acetaminophen as needed.
Discharge meds: augmentation weekly, tiotropium, albuterol prn, icatibant prn.
Plan: outpatient physical therapy 2-3 times weekly; PM&R clinic in 4 months; neurosurgery 6 weeks. No driving until cleared by PM&R.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with his mother, who drove. Hospital and rehab summaries reviewed.

Course: unhelmeted motorcycle crash 12/7, T4 fracture with spinal cord injury, neurogenic shock in the ICU (pressors and atropine, off by 12/11), fusion T2-T6 with T4 laminectomy 12/8 with HAE prophylaxis. Injury proved incomplete. Six weeks of inpatient rehab, home 1/31.

Now: walking indoors with a rolling walker, slow but steady. Bladder working - voiding normally since the catheter came out, no urgency or leaking. Bowels normal. Back pain 3/10, acetaminophen only, off oxycodone since discharge. Mood: frustrated, some low days, but motivated and sleeping. PHQ-9 6. Infusions back on weekly since late December. Breathing at baseline. Working from home part time.

Exam: SpO2 93% RA. Thin, 60 kg. Midline thoracic incision well healed. Hip flexors and knee extensors 4/5 bilaterally, ankles 4+/5. Light touch reduced below the nipple line but present. Gait with walker, narrow-based, no knee buckling. Lungs diminished at baseline. Calves soft.

A/P:
1. Incomplete T4 SCI s/p fusion: improving. PT referral sent to a clinic near home per rehab plan. Neurosurgery visit in March; PM&R in June. No driving until PM&R clears.
2. Neurogenic shock and hypoxemia: resolved - off list.
3. T4 fracture: healing; neurosurgery following.
4. Mood: adjustment to injury, PHQ-9 mild range; supportive talk, he declines counseling for now, will tell me if worse.
5. AATD, HAE, history of testicular cancer: unchanged; oncology aware of the admission.
RTC 3 months.

documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
Outpatient physical therapy. Evaluation 02/17/2025.
Dx: incomplete T4 SCI after fusion T2-T6, home from inpatient rehab 1/31.
Findings: bilateral hip flexor and knee extensor weakness 4/5, mild proximal fatigue after 5 minutes of walking; gait with rolling walker, cadence slow. Balance: needs walker for safety in open spaces. No spasticity limiting function.
Goals: walk community distances without a device in 12 weeks; stairs reciprocal with rail.
Plan: 2-3 visits weekly for gait, balance and strengthening; home program issued. Respiratory pacing with exertion given his emphysema.

reports.conclusion: Intact T2-T6 instrumentation, alignment maintained.

Community hospital emergency department. Date of service: 06/19/2026 (Friday evening).
CC: trouble breathing after a car crash.
HPI: 28-year-old man, belted driver in a high-speed collision. Arrives alert and anxious, short of breath. History: alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with emphysema on weekly augmentation, hereditary angioedema type I, NF1, treated testicular germ cell tumor, T4 spinal cord injury in 2024 with fusion and good recovery.
Meds: alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor weekly IV, tiotropium, albuterol prn, icatibant prn. Allergies: NKDA.
Vitals: BP 130/85, HR 110, RR 28, SpO2 89% on room air.
Exam: no seat-belt sign or other outward chest wall injury; decreased breath sounds on the left. Abdomen soft. Moves all extremities, neuro at his known baseline.
ABG on room air: pH 7.45, PaCO2 32, PaO2 60, HCO3 24.
Chest x-ray: patchy irregular alveolar opacities in the left lung, no rib fractures.
Assessment: left pulmonary contusion with hypoxemia.
Plan: oxygen by nasal cannula, CT chest, trauma admission.

documents.title: Thoracic Surgery Operative Report
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
Community hospital. Date of surgery: 06/21/2026.
Preoperative diagnosis: enlarging left lower lobe pulmonary hematoma (4.8 to 6.3 cm) with worsening oxygenation, after blunt chest trauma.
Procedure: left video-assisted thoracoscopic evacuation of pulmonary hematoma; left chest tube.
HAE prophylaxis: C1 esterase inhibitor concentrate before induction per his allergist's protocol.
Findings: contused left lower lobe with a large organized intraparenchymal hematoma; no active bleeding after evacuation; no air leak on testing. No rib fractures seen.
Three ports. One 24 Fr chest tube. EBL 150 mL. No complications; no angioedema.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Community hospital, trauma service. Admitted 06/19/2026, discharged 06/26/2026 home.
Diagnoses: left pulmonary contusion with intraparenchymal hematoma; hypoxemia.
Course: admitted on 3 L nasal cannula after CT showed a 4.8 cm left lower lobe hematoma within the contusion. On 6/21 needed more oxygen; repeat CT showed the hematoma at 6.3 cm. Thoracic surgery performed left VATS evacuation on 6/21 with C1 inhibitor prophylaxis. Chest tube removed 6/24. Weaned to room air 6/25, SpO2 92% at rest. Augmentation held during admission, to resume next week. Ambulating independently.
Discharge meds: oxycodone 5 mg every 6 h as needed for 5 days; acetaminophen 1 g every 8 h as needed; continue tiotropium, albuterol prn, icatibant prn, weekly augmentation.
Follow-up: PCP within 2 weeks; thoracic surgery in 4 weeks with chest x-ray; pulmonology as scheduled.

Hospital follow-up. ED record, op note and discharge summary reviewed.

Summary: belted driver, high-speed crash 6/19. Arrived hypoxemic (SpO2 89% RA, PaO2 60) with a left lung contusion on x-ray, no rib fractures. CT: 4.8 cm hematoma in the left lower lobe, grew to 6.3 cm by 6/21 with rising oxygen needs; left VATS evacuation 6/21 with C1 inhibitor cover. Chest tube out 6/24, room air 6/25, home 6/26.

Now: breathing close to his usual; albuterol once a day, down from twice. Mild left chest soreness 2/10, finished the oxycodone, acetaminophen as needed. No fever, cough or sputum. No swelling episodes. Augmentation restarted 6/29. Working from home. Not driving yet - wants to wait until after thoracic surgery sees him. Mood okay, shaken by a second crash; PHQ-9 4.

Exam: SpO2 92% RA (his usual 92-94). Weight 62 kg. Port sites on the left chest healing, no erythema. Lungs: breath sounds slightly decreased at the left base, otherwise his baseline diminished sounds; no crackles. Heart RRR. Calves soft.

A/P:
1. Left pulmonary contusion with hematoma s/p VATS evacuation: recovering. Thoracic surgery 7/28 with chest x-ray. Return precautions: fever, worsening breathlessness, chest pain, coughing blood.
2. Hypoxemia: resolved, back at baseline saturation - off list.
3. AATD with emphysema: augmentation resumed; pulm visit due in August.
4. HAE: no perioperative swelling.
5. CBC and BMP today.
6. Physical due in September.

documents.title: Labs from Friday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Jacob, your blood count and chemistry from Friday came back normal - no anemia after the surgery, kidneys and electrolytes fine. Keep going as you are and let us know how the thoracic surgery visit goes.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Small residual opacity at the left lung base, improved compared with 06/25/2026. Postsurgical changes along the left lateral chest. No pneumothorax. No effusion. Known hyperlucent, bullous lower lobes. Thoracic spinal hardware intact.
reports.conclusion: Improving small residual left basilar opacity after hematoma evacuation.

documents.title: Thoracic Surgery Follow-up
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
Outside thoracic surgery group. Visit 07/28/2026, 5 weeks after left VATS evacuation of pulmonary hematoma.
Recovering well. Mild left chest wall soreness only. Port sites healed.
Chest x-ray: small residual opacity at the left base, improving.
Plan: may return to desk work, which he has. No heavy lifting for 2 more weeks. Return as needed; pulmonology to follow the residual opacity.

documents.title: Back to walking?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thoracic surgery said I'm healing fine. Is it okay to get back to my long walks and light weights, or should I wait for pulmonary in a couple weeks?

documents.title: RE: Back to walking?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Walking is fine now, build up gradually. Hold the weights until after the two weeks thoracic surgery mentioned, then start light. If you get more short of breath than usual, stop and let us know.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group. Visit 08/17/2026.
AATD PiZZ with panlobular emphysema; left pulmonary contusion with hematoma after a June car crash, VATS evacuation 6/21. Back on weekly augmentation since 6/29. Breathing nearly back to baseline. SpO2 92% RA. Exam: slightly decreased sounds left base.
Plan: continue augmentation, tiotropium daily, albuterol as needed. Recheck full PFTs and chest x-ray in 3 months, after the contusion has fully cleared.

documents.title: Refill request - icatibant
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Specialty pharmacy sent an electronic refill request for icatibant 30 mg syringes to our office. Prescriber of record is the allergist. Forwarded to the allergy office and let pharmacy know.
